2.content:
This SOW covers Alcon’s fixed-price technical conversion of its SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise, including migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux, mandatory simplification remediation under a no-change principle, testing, cutover, hypercare, and transition to AMS across 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants, with planned go-live in February 2028 and a production downtime target of no more than 48 hours.

- Execute the ECC to S/4HANA technical conversion and platform migration using a no-change approach limited to mandatory simplification items.
- Deliver a downtime-optimized conversion, test cycle, and cutover plan to support February 2028 go-live within the agreed production downtime target.
- Remediate and qualify impacted custom code, integrations, security, and analytics components required for business continuity after conversion.

Deferred scope decisions, delivery assumptions, and dependency conditions are set out in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

4.1.content: The services cover Alcon’s SAP landscape across 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants. Delivery will be performed through a mix of on-site and distributed execution across the USA, North America, EMEA, and APAC, including activities supporting the Fort Worth distribution centers. The production conversion and cutover scope applies to the in-scope global template, regional entities, and manufacturing operations included in the current ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape.

4.2.content: In-scope business process areas are limited to the processes affected by the technical conversion and mandatory SAP simplification remediation under the no-change principle. These include Finance, Equipment Finance Agreements, Technical Services, MM, STRM (WM), SD/OTI, PP, and MDG. Process continuity validation, change impact validation, user acceptance support, training support, and communications support are included only to the extent required to enable the technical conversion, qualification, and go-live readiness of the in-scope SAP processes.

4.3.content:
Technical scope includes conversion of Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise and migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6. The scope includes SUM/DMO downtime-optimized conversion with CustOnTemp, sandbox and development screening, mandatory simplification remediation, remediation of in-scope development objects, update of security framework, add-ons and bolt-ons, formal quality test cycles, backup/DR/HA technical testing, 10 conversion cycles consisting of 2 standard and 8 mock runs, technical load verification, dress rehearsal, production conversion, and hypercare support. The technical baseline for remediation and qualification includes custom code, integrations, BW on HANA, Datasphere, SAC, BODS, BASIS, security, and ABAP components required for business continuity after go-live. The current remediation and qualification baseline comprises 22,765 custom code objects and 1,114 integration objects, based on the approved technical inventory as of March 2026.

<IMAGE id="42e72067b696"/>

4.4.content: Included services are program and project management, conversion planning, solution and technical architecture, environment and conversion strategy definition, remediation planning and execution for in-scope technical objects, test planning and test support, cutover planning and execution, deployment support, hypercare through March 2028, and transition support to AMS. The services also include governance, status reporting, RACI-based delivery coordination, change and communication support, training support, and user feedback and adoption tracking where required for the conversion program. OCM support is included in line with the agreed delivery plan and resource mobilization schedule.

4.5.content:
Application scope is limited to the in-scope SAP applications and functional areas required for the technical conversion program: SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise, Finance, Equipment Finance Agreements, Technical Services, MM, STRM (WM), SD/OTI, PP, MDG, BASIS, Security, ABAP, and analytics components comprising BW, Datasphere, SAC, and BODS. Application changes are restricted to mandatory SAP simplification items and remediation necessary to preserve existing business functionality under the no-change principle.

3.1.content:
Alcon is undertaking a fixed-price technical conversion of its SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise across 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants. The program includes migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux, mandatory simplification remediation under a no-change principle, testing, cutover, hypercare, and transition to AMS.

The current landscape presents scale, technical complexity, and downtime risk. Key delivery pain points include the volume of custom code, integrations, and analytics objects requiring remediation, the need to validate mandatory simplification impacts without introducing elective change, and the requirement to execute production conversion within a maximum 48-hour downtime window. Business drivers for this engagement are platform modernization, improved operational resilience, reduction of the technical downtime footprint through iterative mock cycles and load verification, and readiness for stable post-conversion operations on SAP S/4HANA.

3.2.content:
- Convert Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise using a no-change approach limited to mandatory simplification items.
- Migrate the database and platform from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6.
- Remediate and qualify impacted custom code, integrations, security components, and analytics assets required for business continuity.
- Execute 10 conversion cycles, including mock conversions, load verification, dress rehearsal, and production cutover.
- Achieve February 2028 go-live within the agreed production downtime target of no more than 48 hours.
- Complete hypercare and transition the stabilized solution into AMS support.

3.3.content:
The target-state delivery model follows a controlled technical conversion path from pre-planning through sandbox and landscape preparation, iterative conversion and validation cycles, downtime optimization, production cutover, hypercare, and transition to AMS. Each cycle is intended to reduce technical risk, improve cutover predictability, and confirm conversion readiness across infrastructure, application, security, integration, and analytics layers.

<IMAGE id="c8d8e19bae62"/>

In the to-be state, Alcon operates on SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise on HANA 2.0 and Red Hat Linux with mandatory simplification items remediated, qualified business processes across in-scope functions, and a cutover approach proven through repeated mock execution. The delivery approach culminates in February 2028 production conversion, one month of hypercare, and structured handover to AMS.

5.content:
The proposed solution architecture is a no-change SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise target state for Alcon’s current ECC 6.0 Ehp6 landscape, with conversion limited to mandatory simplification items and technical remediation required to preserve existing business continuity. The architecture includes migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6, remediation and qualification of in-scope custom code, integrations, security components, and analytics assets, and execution of SUM/DMO downtime-optimized conversion with CustOnTemp to support the agreed production downtime target of no more than 48 hours.

The deployment model is a phased technical-conversion approach across sandbox, development, quality, mock, load-verification, dress-rehearsal, and production environments, culminating in February 2028 go-live and March 2028 hypercare. Architecture execution will be validated through 10 conversion cycles, including mock conversions, technical load verification, backup/DR/HA testing, and cutover rehearsal to confirm performance, stability, and readiness of the converted landscape across the in-scope global footprint.

<IMAGE id="bd5f7d275ef9"/>

Change governance for the architecture will follow a centralized and integrated program model aligned to Alcon governance and RMO oversight, with defined daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadences for delivery control, escalation, risk management, and decision-making. Ownership will be structured through clear technical and functional accountability, track-level leadership, defined multi-vendor interaction boundaries, and formal change control for any deviation from the no-change principle, approved technical baseline, or agreed downtime and validation approach.

Where required for regulated delivery, the architecture and deployment model will be executed in alignment with Alcon’s validation and lifecycle controls, including qualification, traceability, change control, release readiness, and audit-ready documentation standards. <TECH TEAM: confirm whether an environment-level architecture diagram for infrastructure, HANA, DR, and interface connectivity should be inserted here in addition to the delivery-team structure visual>

6.1.content:
The engagement will be executed as a fixed-price technical conversion using a no-change delivery model limited to mandatory SAP simplification items and technical remediation required for business continuity. Delivery will proceed through month-zero pre-planning, sandbox and landscape screening, environment preparation, iterative conversion cycles, qualification, downtime optimization, cutover rehearsal, production conversion, hypercare, and transition to AMS.

The methodology uses SUM/DMO downtime-optimized conversion with CustOnTemp, supported by 10 conversion cycles comprising standard and mock runs, technical load verification, backup/DR/HA testing, and a final dress rehearsal to validate the February 2028 go-live and the production downtime target of no more than 48 hours. Quality control will be enforced through phase-based Q-Gates, continuous delivery assessments, RAID governance, weekly status reviews, and formal readiness checks before deployment. Where required for regulated processes, execution will align with Alcon validation and lifecycle controls for qualification, traceability, release readiness, and audit-ready documentation.

7.1.content:
The engagement will follow a centralized and integrated governance model aligned to Alcon’s RMO structure, with shared oversight across Alcon, Bristlecone, and other participating partners. Governance will operate through delivery, management, and executive layers to control scope, schedule, risks, quality, financials, and cross-track dependencies for the fixed-price technical conversion.

Day-to-day execution will be managed by the Program Manager, Project Manager, core functional and technical leads, and Cutover/Test leadership through daily stand-ups and internal team meetings. Weekly PMO meetings will review plan status, risks, issues, decisions, and actions. Monthly Steering Committee meetings will address milestone readiness, major risks, scope or timeline impacts, and executive decisions requiring cross-functional alignment. Ad hoc meetings may be convened where urgent resolution is required.

Escalation will follow a three-level path: Level 1 through the Project Manager and core solution team for delivery issues, Level 2 through the Program Manager for cross-track, dependency, or schedule impacts, and Level 3 through client and delivery leadership for matters affecting scope, commercials, governance decisions, or go-live readiness.

10.content:
- The engagement is limited to a no-change technical conversion from SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise, and only mandatory SAP simplification items and remediation required for business continuity are in scope.
- Elective business, process, functional, reporting, integration, or technical enhancements are excluded and any deviation from the no-change principle will require approval through the Change Management Process.
- The fixed-price baseline, remediation effort, and delivery plan are based on the approved technical inventory as of March 2026, including 22,765 custom code objects and 1,114 integration objects.
- Any increase in object volumes, interface scope, analytics remediation scope, add-on or bolt-on remediation, or country, entity, plant, or business-process scope beyond the agreed baseline will be handled through the Change Management Process.
- Alcon will lead source-system preparation and provide timely support for required system builds, refreshes, environment readiness, access, and client-owned technical prerequisites.
- Delivery will proceed on the agreed phase plan from June 2026 through March 2028, with month zero reserved for pre-planning and mobilization, February 2028 go-live, and one month of hypercare through March 2028.
- Production conversion planning, mock cycles, technical load verification, and cutover activities are based on an agreed business downtime target of no more than 48 hours.
- Bristlecone’s OCM and change-support deliverable frequency and intensity depend on the agreed mobilization date of the Bristlecone OCM resource and alignment to Alcon’s CCM methodology.
- Client reviews, decisions, defect triage, validation approvals, and sign-offs will be provided in line with the project schedule to avoid impact to conversion cycles, qualification, cutover readiness, and go-live.
- Where regulated processes apply, Alcon will provide and govern the required validation framework, standards, approvals, and controlled documentation inputs needed for compliant execution across qualification, traceability, release readiness, and audit-ready records.
- Any change to the agreed scope, baseline assumptions, delivery dependencies, schedule, downtime target, or client responsibilities set out in this SOW will be managed through the Change Management Process described in Section 17.

17.content:
Any change to the agreed scope, fixed-price baseline, object inventory, schedule, downtime target, deliverables, assumptions, client dependencies, or responsibilities shall be managed through the formal Change Request (CR) process below. No out-of-scope work, elective change, or baseline increase will be performed without written approval through this process. Approved CRs shall be reflected in the applicable project controls, including plan, RAID, deliverables, commercials, and acceptance baselines.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | Bristlecone or Alcon project lead identifies the proposed change, states the reason, and records the affected scope, baseline, milestone, dependency, or acceptance item. | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | Bristlecone Project Manager logs the CR, assigns a tracking ID, classifies the impact area, and circulates it to the required reviewers. | Within 1 business day of CR receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | Bristlecone assesses scope, effort, schedule, downtime, environment, testing, validation, cutover, and commercial impact; Alcon confirms client-side dependency impact and decision inputs. | Within 5 business days of logging, unless the parties agree a different period for major changes |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | Alcon PMO, authorized Alcon approver(s), and Bristlecone Program Manager review the assessment and approve, reject, or defer the CR. No change is effective until written approval is issued. | Within 5 business days of impact assessment submission |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | For an approved CR, the parties update the SOW, milestone plan, deliverables, commercials, or other affected baseline documents as required before implementation. | Before execution of the approved change |
| 6 | CR closure | Bristlecone Project Manager updates the CR log with final status, links the approved amendment or decision record, and confirms implementation or closure. | Within 2 business days of implementation decision or completion |

Changes requiring a CR include any deviation from the no-change principle; increases beyond the March 2026 baseline inventory of custom code, integration, or analytics objects; changes affecting the February 2028 go-live plan or March 2028 hypercare completion; changes to the agreed production downtime target of no more than 48 hours; and any client or third-party dependency that impacts delivery, validation, cutover, or acceptance. Where regulated processes apply, CR review and implementation shall align with Alcon validation and lifecycle controls, including traceability, controlled documentation, and approval requirements.

- Maintain a baselined milestone deliverables matrix that ties each major phase, deliverable, acceptance event, and invoice trigger to named owners and review windows.
